subject: Categorical variables (have been converted to dummy variables) as covariate variables in a SEM model

messages.author: e3973a682064049e
messages.subject: Categorical variables (have been converted to dummy variables) as covariate variables in a SEM model
parts:
Hi there,

I am using a categorical variable (3 levels) as a covariate (independent/exogenous variable) in my sem model.

Since I know,  this variable is needed to be recorded as a dummy (K-1) variable.

I did this by model.matrix() function. I checked the results, and I got the two (k-1) new dummy variables.
res <- model.matrix(~Category, data = data)
head(res)
head(res[, -1])


Then I run my sem model:
semModel <- "
   ...
   #covariates
   v1 + v2 ~ Category"

It still shows 'lavaan ERROR: unordered factor(s) with more than 2 levels detected as exogenous covariate(s): Category' 

Any ideas will be appreciated.

Best,
Serena

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Categorical variables (have been converted to dummy variables) as covariate variables in a SEM model
parts:
This is not a full reprex, but you should just make straight-forward dummy codes as new variables in the data.frame that you pass to lavaan(data=).

data$cat1 <- ifelse(data$Category == "first", yes = 1, no = 0)
data$cat2 <- ifelse(data$Category == "second", yes = 1, no = 0)

Then add those numeric dummy codes to your lavaan syntax, not the original nominal factor.

messages.subject: Re: Categorical variables (have been converted to dummy variables) as covariate variables in a SEM model
parts:
Dear all,

I'm trying to use a categorical variable with three levels as a covariate in a bivariate latent change score model. This variable, named "set_order" in my dataframe, corresponds to the order of different sets of items seen by participants at pretest and posttest. The orders are: A,C; B,A; and C,B. I do not want to analyze this variable directly but want to control for it as the sets have different levels of difficulty and participants are unbalalanced accross the different order.

In a mixed model approach, we used sum coding contrast (so that the intercept represents the mean between conditions) to control for the set order, and I would like to apply this method to my SEM analysis.

I created two variables for the two contrasts (k-1) in my dataframe:

  • Contrast 1: "A,C" = -1, "B,A" = 1, "C,B" = 0
  • Contrast 2: "A,C" = -1, "B,A" = 0, "C,B" = 1

I then used these variables in my lavaan syntax. However, I am facing two problems:

  1. I received this error message:
Warning in lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats, : lavaan WARNING: The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov) does not appear to be positive definite! The smallest eigenvalue (= 1.119753e-19) is close to zero. This may be a symptom that the model is not identified.
  1. The model does not fit (it fits very well without the contrast variables): χ² (6) = 431, p < 0.000, CFI = 0.75, TLI = -0.15, RMSEA = 0.199, SRMR = 0.07

Any advice on how to resolve these issues would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you so much!

Marine

PhD student in developmental psychology - Université paris Cité

messages.subject: Re: Categorical variables (have been converted to dummy variables) as covariate variables in a SEM model
parts:
1. I received this error message:
Warning in lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats, : lavaan WARNING: The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov) does not appear to be positive definite! The smallest eigenvalue (= 1.119753e-19) is close to zero. This may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

This is a warning, not an error.  You did not provide a reproducible example (reprex), but I'm guessing you estimated intercepts?  For codes like this, their mean and variance are not independently defined.  It is simple to avoid the warning with dummy codes by labeling them both and constraining the variance to be the mean times 1 minus the mean (consistent with the Bernoulli distribution).  But it is less straight-forward for effects codes that can have 3 values.  Regardless, you can probably ignore the warning.
1. The model does not fit (it fits very well without the contrast variables): χ² (6) = 431, p < 0.000, CFI = 0.75, TLI = -0.15, RMSEA = 0.199, SRMR = 0.07
Without a reprex, it is difficult to guess why.

parts:
Dear Dr. Jorgensen,

Thank you for your initial reply. I will try to provide a reprex and be as clear as possible.

My experiment is a classic intervention design with a pretest and a posttest. Participants took two tasks (measuring two distinct concepts, X and Y) at pretest and posttest. Initially, I analyzed my data using a mixed model approach, which shows an improvement between pretest and posttest on both tasks while controlling for three variables:

  • Age: Continuous variable
  • Sex: Recoded as - 0.5 and 0.5
  • Order (depicting the set of items seen at pretest and posttest): Three levels, recoded using sum contrasts coding.

Now, I would like to use a bivariate latent change score model as described by Kievit et al. (2018) to investigate three things while controlling for age, sex, and order:

  1. Relationship between changes in Y and X
  2. Baseline effects: The impact of the baseline of Y on Y's latent change and the baseline of X on X's latent change.
  3. Coupling effects: The impact of the baseline of X on Y's latent change and the baseline of Y on X's latent change.

I have attached an image of my theoretical model and see below the lavaan syntax of the model (adapted from Kievit et al. (2018)).

The main issue here is how to control for my set order variable with three levels. I do not want to analyze this variable directly but want to control for it as the sets have different levels of difficulty and participants are unbalalanced accross the different order.

First model tested with order as ordinal variable:

- The order variable was recoded as an ordinal variable with the value of 1,2,3 ( order_1 = 1,  order_2 = 2,  order_3 =3) and integrated in my lavaan syntax.

- The model fitted well : Chi2 (df = 3) = 0.16 , P = 0.984, RMSEA = 0.000, CFI = 1.000, SRMR = 0.002

However I am not sure wether the estimate of my model are correct as order is a nominal variable and that I want to estimate the parameters for the mean of the different order (In a regression model, I have to set a sum coding contrast to this variable for the parameter to be interpretable).

Second model tested with order separate in two contrast variables (sum coding) :

Here are some details about my data :

- Y_PRE : baseline of Y at pretest centered, continuous variable

- Y_POST : level of Y at posttest centered on PRE, continuous variable

- X_PRE : baseline of X at pretest centered, continuous variable

- X_POST : level of X at posttest centered on PRE, continuous variable

- Age : age of participant centered, continuous variable

- Sex : sex of participant, recoded 0.5 and -0.5

The order variable is recoded into 2 contrast variables using sum contrast coding :

- Order_C1 : first contrast variable of order, with order_1 = -1,  order_2 = 1,  order_3 = 0

- Order_C2 : second contrast variable of order, with order_1 = -1,  order_2 = 0,  order_3 = 1

Here the lavaan syntax of my model :

BLCS <- " 
########## create latent change score in Y (dY) ##########
## regression    
Y_POST ~ 1*Y_PRE  # Regression of PRE on POST with a coefficient fixed to 1
dY =~ 1*Y_POST    # Regression of POST on Y latent change score with a coefficient fixed to 1
dY ~ Y_PRE        # Regression of PRE on  Y latent change score with a free coefficient

## intercept and variance of observed variables
Y_POST ~ 0*1            # Intercept fixed to 0
Y_POST ~~ 0*crt_POST    # Variance  fixed to 0
Y_PRE ~ 1               # Intercept is free
Y_PRE ~~ Y_PRE          # Variance is free

## intercept and variance of Y latent change score
dY ~ 1              # Intercept is free
dY ~~ dY               # Variance is free  

########## create latent change score in X (dX) ##########
##  regression        
X_POST ~ 1*X_PRE     # Regression of PRE on POST with a coefficient fixed to 1
dX =~ 1*X_POST       # Regression of POST on X latent change score with a coefficient fixed to 1
dX ~ X_PRE           # Regression of PRE on  X latent change score with a free coefficient

## intercept and variance of observed variables
X_POST ~ 0*1           # Intercept fixed to 0
X_POST ~~ 0*X_POST     # Variance  fixed to 0
X_PRE ~ 1              # Intercept is free
X_PRE ~~ X_PRE         # Variance is free

## intercept and variance of X latent change score
dX ~ 1               # Intercept is free
dX ~~ dX             # Variance is free      

##########  intercept and variance of controlled variables  ##########
 AGE ~ 1                 # Intercept is free
 AGE ~~ AGE              # Variance is free

 SEX ~ 1                 # Intercept is free
 SEX ~~ SEX              # Variance is free
 
 ORDER_C1 ~ 1            # Intercept is free
 ORDER_C1 ~~ ORDER_C1    # Variance is free
 
 ORDER_C2 ~ 1            # Intercept is free
 ORDER_C2 ~~ ORDER_C2    # Variance is free

########## Regressions on latent variables dX & dY ##########
dY ~ X_PRE + AGE + SEX + ORDER_C1 + ORDER_C2   
dX ~ Y_PRE + AGE + SEX + ORDER_C1 + ORDER_C2   

########## Regressions of controlled variables on baselines : Y_PRE & X_PRE ##########
Y_PRE ~ AGE + SEX + ORDER_C1 + ORDER_C2
X_PRE ~ AGE + SEX + ORDER_C1 + ORDER_C2

########## covariances ##########

Y_PRE ~~ X_PRE
dY ~~ dX
"

Here the code to run this model :

fitBLCS = sem(BLCS,data=data, estimator='mlr',missing='fiml',fixed.x = FALSE)

summary(fitBLCS,rsquare = TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized = TRUE)

 Model  fit :  χ² (6) = 431, p < 0.000, CFI = 0.75, TLI = -0.15, RMSEA = 0.199, SRMR = 0.07

I hope these details help clarify my situation. Please let me know if you need any additional information. Thank you very much for your time and assistance.

Marine

messages.subject: Re: Categorical variables (have been converted to dummy variables) as covariate variables in a SEM model
parts: Your exogenous variables (sex, order) are not normally distributed, so you should not estimate their means or (co)variances in the syntax.  Leave the default setting (fixed.x=TRUE), but if any of the exogenous predictors are incomplete, you can set <font face="Courier New">missing = "fiml.x"</font>
